riskReasons: RHS, Missouri Botanical Garden and a documented living collection consistently support the accepted name and Acer palmatum placement.
The var. dissectum and Dissectum Group formulations describe horticultural placement rather than separate identities.
Published size and autumn-colour emphasis vary modestly, but no material identity or synonym conflict remains.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with RC-001–RC-010 and all other approved Catalogue assignments. ‘Waterfall’ is distinct from the generic Dissectum Viride Group and from unnamed green laceleaf maples; it is also distinct from upright RC-002 ‘Seiryu’ and the red dissectum profiles CUL-000013 and CUL-000020. C0 resolves as unique.

identityNotes: The Atlas uses Acer palmatum ‘Waterfall’. Var. dissectum and Dissectum Group formulations are retained as horticultural placement and search variants, not separate cultivar identities. Generic ‘green laceleaf’ descriptions are insufficient to identify this cultivar.

content.summary: A green laceleaf Japanese maple forming a dense, cascading mound, with deeply dissected foliage that remains green through summer and develops a bright mixture of yellow, gold, orange and red in autumn.
content.habit: Pendulous, weeping shrub or small tree with cascading branches and a broad, mounded crown. It commonly spreads wider than it grows tall and can be trained to show more trunk.
content.leafForm: Fine, feathery dissectum foliage with narrow, deeply cut lobes divided to or near the leaf base. Missouri Botanical Garden describes seven to nine lobes and slightly longer leaves than generic green dissectum forms.

seasonal.spring: Fresh foliage emerges bright green; early growth can be vulnerable to late spring frost in exposed sites.
seasonal.summer: Leaves remain bright to dark green, forming a dense lace-like canopy when moisture is adequate.
seasonal.autumn: Foliage turns golden yellow with showy orange and red streaks; the balance of colours varies by site and season.

size.qualifier: RHS gives 1.5–2.5 m high and 2.5–4 m wide; Missouri Botanical Garden gives 6–10 ft high and 8–12 ft wide. JC Raulston Arboretum records two plants measured at 7 ft in 2023.

content.cultivation: Grow in moisture-retentive, well-drained, preferably slightly acidic soil in a sheltered position. Part shade is dependable; full sun may be tolerated where soil stays reliably moist. Protect the fine foliage from drying wind and hot, dry exposure.
content.diagnostic: The combination of a broad cascading mound, green deeply dissected leaves and multicoloured yellow-orange-red autumn display supports comparison with ‘Waterfall’. It must not be inferred from any generic green laceleaf plant, and it is not the upright dissectum RC-002 ‘Seiryu’.
content.confidence: High confidence in accepted name, taxon, dissectum placement, cascading habit and broad seasonal sequence. Moderate confidence in ultimate dimensions and the precise autumn-colour balance because the institutional ranges and site observations differ.
content.unresolvedIssue: The lean review does not establish a single universal size ceiling or a quantitative leaf-length threshold separating ‘Waterfall’ from every green dissectum cultivar.
